processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Four ingots of the Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C-xNi-yCr series (x = 0, 2 wt%; y = 0, 3, 5 wt%) were prepared; the 2Ni3Cr ingot is one of them.
As-cast ingots homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h.
Hot-rolled to 4 mm-thick sheets with 95% thickness reduction.

processing_steps.cooling_medium: water (efficient-use-water ultrafast-cooled device ADCOS-PM, developed in-house)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Plate online ultrafast cooled to ambient temperature at ~40 °C/s.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized single equiaxed FCC γ (austenite) structure with a high fraction of Σ3 twin boundaries, plus nanoscale κ-carbide/LRO ordered domains; no B2 phase with BCC structure was found by EBSD or XRD.

phases_present.grain_size: 8.57 μm (excluding twin boundaries); 3.72 μm (including twin boundaries)

defects.type: high fraction of Σ3 twin boundaries

phases_present.phase_name: κ-carbide (ordered E21-type structure) / LRO ordered domains
phases_present.crystal_structure: orthorhombic (as stated for the 2Ni3Cr κ-carbides); perovskite E21 structure for κ-carbide
phases_present.volume_fraction: very low (not quantified; DF thickness uncertain prevented quantitative estimate)

precipitates.distribution: distributed in the γ matrix; homogeneous fine bright particles in dark-field TEM

interfaces.phase_evolution: Cr added to the Fe–Mn–Al–C matrix takes the place of Al to form (Fe, Mn)CrC and raises the formation energy of κ-carbides as well as the interfacial and elastic strain energies between κ-carbides and the γ austenite matrix, increasing the nucleation energy barrier and thereby decreasing κ-carbide size; Ni lowers the formation energy and nucleation barrier of κ-carbides (AlNi3C), promoting their growth. In 2Ni3Cr both effects coexist.
interfaces.interface_notes: Quantitative volume fraction of κ-carbides could not be estimated from dark-field imaging because the sheet thickness is uncertain.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge length 25 mm, thickness 3 mm, width 7 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: crosshead speed 3 mm/min on a Gotech electronic universal testing machine with laser extensometer; specimens cut by EDM along the rolling direction (RD); at least three specimens per steel deformed to fracture

comparative_performance.benchmark_alloy_id: alloy_fe-20mn-9al-1.5c-3cr (3Cr steel, no added Ni, same HR+UFC process)
comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield strength (YS): 2Ni3Cr steel has a yield strength increase of ~141 MPa compared to 3Cr steel
2Ni3Cr steel achieves YS exceeding 1100 MPa, UTS surpassing 1200 MPa and TEL greater than 45%, breaking the conventional strength–ductility trade-off

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Ultra55 scanning electron microscope; specimens vibration polished with 50 nm colloidal silica for 2.5–24 h (Buehler-VibroMet 2)
characterization_methods.purpose: determine phase constitution and average grain size (with/without twin boundaries)
characterization_methods.key_findings: 2Ni3Cr steel is fully recrystallized single equiaxed FCC γ (phase map uniformly red) with a high fraction of Σ3 twin boundaries; average grain size 8.57 μm (excluding twins) and 3.72 μm (including twins); no B2/BCC phase.
Only five FCC γ reflections (γ(111), γ(200), γ(220), γ(311), γ(222)); no reflection attributable to a B2/BCC phase, confirming single-phase γ austenite for 2Ni3Cr.

characterization_methods.technique: transmission electron microscopy (TEM) bright-field and dark-field, selected area diffraction (SAED)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Tecnai G2 F20 operating at 200 kV; specimens thinned with Struers TenuPol-3 double-jet (10 vol% perchloric acid + 90 vol% ethanol, 20 V, -30 °C)
characterization_methods.purpose: reveal γ grains, twins, and nanoscale κ-carbide/LRO ordered domains
characterization_methods.key_findings: 2Ni3Cr microstructure is γ austenite; SAED shows weak κ superlattice spots (011κ, 100κ); dark-field ({110}κ reflection) reveals fine bright κ-carbide/ordered particles of intermediate size; κ-carbides are orthorhombic with cuboidal morphology.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: [011]γ zone axis; FFT patterns; IFFT reconstructed using {011} and {100} LRO superlattice reflections
characterization_methods.purpose: image and size the κ-carbides/LRO domains
characterization_methods.key_findings: 2Ni3Cr κ-carbides/LRO domains have an average size of ~5.46 nm (measured over >200 domains by Image-Pro Plus).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM of fracture surface fibre zone
characterization_methods.key_findings: 2Ni3Cr fracture surface shows a dimpled microvoid-coalescence morphology (ductile fracture), with the finest and most uniform dimple population of the four steels.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: calculation of possible (κ-)carbide structures and their formation energies for the Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.5C steel family
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Trends (Cr raises and Ni lowers κ-carbide formation energy / nucleation barrier) used to explain the dark-field TEM sizes (Fig. 1i-1l) and κ-carbide size sequence.

analytical_models.model_name: First-principles formation energies of possible (κ-)carbides structures
analytical_models.equation_role: assess stability and equilibrium of κ-carbides and Ni/Cr-rich carbides
analytical_models.model_note: Cr-rich carbide Cr21(FeC3)2 (−0.049) is 0.111 eV/atom higher than the common (Fe, Mn)AlC κ-carbide, increasing the nucleation energy barrier; AlNi3C (−0.181) is lower than ideal κ-carbide, lowering the barrier and promoting κ-carbide formation.

computational_details.simulation_method: analytical strengthening model (linear superposition of strengthening mechanisms)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: fully recrystallized Fe–Mn–Al–C steel; contribution of dislocation strengthening disregarded; precipitation strengthening taken as the larger of σ_order and (σ_coh + σ_mod)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated yield strengths compared with measured tensile yield strengths (Fig. 11); good agreement with experimental values.

analytical_models.model_note: σ_prep for 2Ni3Cr is dominated by σ_coh + σ_mod (Fig. 10c: dense cluster ~1.5–2.6 nm peaking near 23 MPa plus isolated taller bars near 3.6 and 3.9 nm reaching ~27 and ~29 MPa).

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of 2Ni3Cr steel (wt.%, Table 1): C 1.41, Si 0.35, Mn 20.3, P 0.009, S 0.002, Al 8.63, Mo 0.53, Ni 2.11, Cr 2.89, Ti 0.01, Nb 0.03, Fe Bal.
TS × TEL (product of tensile strength and total elongation) for the 2Ni3Cr steel = 55.36 GPa-% (Table 2).
Average size of the κ-carbide/LRO ordered domains in 2Ni3Cr steel ≈ 5.46 nm (measured over more than 200 domains using Image-Pro Plus software).
κ-carbides in 2Ni3Cr steel are described as orthorhombic with a cuboidal morphology distributed in the γ matrix.
Average grain size of 2Ni3Cr steel is 8.57 μm excluding twin boundaries and 3.72 μm including twin boundaries; the effective grain size d_eff used in the strengthening model is 3.72 μm.
Across 2Ni → 2Ni3Cr → 2Ni5Cr, Cr addition decreases yield strength from 1202 to 1071 MPa and tensile strength from 1283 to 1187 MPa, while total elongation increases from 34.1% to 54.5%.

In strain-hardening behavior, Stage II is prolonged and Stage III shows a higher work-hardening rate for 2Ni3Cr steel than for the 2Ni steel with increasing Cr content; with increasing Ni (3Cr → 2Ni3Cr), Stages II and III are shortened and lowered.

The 2Ni3Cr steel was one of a 4-ingot series Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C-xNi-yCr (x = 0, 2 wt%; y = 0, 3, 5 wt%) all subject to the identical hot-rolling + online ultrafast cooling (UFC) route with ~40 °C/s cooling and 95% hot-rolling reduction to 4 mm sheets.
